verdict.line: You lose if you walk into Q-E poke chains at range; you win once you force him into melee Cannon Stance and land a stun.

brief.thesis: Jayce wants to fight you from 600-1200 range in Hammer Stance, poke with Q (To the Skies!) and E (Thundering Blow) without ever entering your W (Frenzied Maul) threat range. Volibear's actual win condition is closing that gap with Q (Thundering Smash) and using E (Sky Splitter) at 1200 range to punish his melee Cannon Stance form instead of trying to out-poke him. The 52.7% win rate over 146 games says this favors you slightly once you play the gap-close correctly, despite Jayce holding the raw lane and solo-kill edge.

theirWindow.when: He's in Hammer Stance at range
theirWindow.what: He can land Q (To the Skies!) leap-slow and E (Thundering Blow) knockback from well outside your W threat range. Do not walk forward to trade here; let him burn Q's 16/14/12/10/8s cooldown on a poke rather than a stun setup.

yourWindow.when: He's in Cannon Stance or just used Q
yourWindow.what: Cannon Stance is his melee-less ranged form but it also means his Hammer-side mobility (the Q leap) is down for 16-8s. Use Q (Thundering Smash) to close instantly and chain into W (Frenzied Maul) twice for the heal.

start.why: Picked in 59.6% of games (53.2% win rate over 109 games) because sustain and mana regen let you tank Jayce's early poke without backing off lane.

boots.why: 62.4% pick rate at 52.3% win rate over 111 games; the attack-speed reduction on his Q-E auto-poke chain directly offsets his damage profile.

core.why: Appears in both top core paths; the on-hit proc plus W (Frenzied Maul) mark gives you a reason to actually land autos through his kiting.
Shows up in the top two core paths (50% and 7.8%/5.8% pick); the active-use sustain keeps you alive through extended Q-E poke exchanges.
Part of the second core path; stacks with Lethal Tempo to shrink your Q (Thundering Smash) and W cooldowns for more gap-close attempts per fight.

runes.keystoneWhy: Run in both listed rune pages (15% and 9.1% pick) because it rewards landing autos during your W (Frenzied Maul) double-cast window, scaling your DPS once you close the gap.

summoners.why: Exhaust+Flash is the highest win rate pairing in this matchup (62.5% over a 21.4% pick rate); Exhaust directly cuts Jayce's poke damage and kiting speed during your Q (Thundering Smash) all-in.

playing.title: Hold position in Hammer Stance
playing.detail: Do not approach while he's at range in Hammer Stance; his Q (To the Skies!) and E (Thundering Blow) both outrange your Q (300) and W (325). Wait for him to commit or swap stance.

playing.title: Punish Cannon Stance commitment
playing.detail: When he swaps to Cannon Stance to poke or farm, his mobility tool (Hammer Q leap) is gone. This is your window to close with Q (Thundering Smash) and land the stun.

playing.title: Save E for his dive, not for poke trades
playing.detail: E (Sky Splitter) has a 16s cooldown and 1200 range; hold it to slow him mid-leap or mid-retreat rather than throwing it into empty space for chip damage.

playing.title: Double-tap W for sustain
playing.detail: W (Frenzied Maul) heals you on the second cast against the same marked target. Always follow up your first W with a second before he can kite away.

playing.title: Time R around his Cannon-form burst window
playing.detail: R (Stormbringer) disables nearby towers temporarily on landing; use it to force a trade under his tower once you're ahead, since his Cannon Stance lacks the Hammer E knockback to peel you off.

playing.title: Track his Q cooldown after every poke
playing.detail: His Q (To the Skies!) drops from 16s to 8s by level 5-9; count it down after each cast so you know exactly when he loses his disengage/leap tool and can be cornered.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the win-condition reading and timing calls are my own tactical judgment, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit with Jayce’s (Q)-(E) pokes. Use [E] to contest lane while using [Q] to close in to gain the upper hand in combat.
